title: Cold rebuild: the token bucket
summary: Rebuild the token bucket with an injected clock from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove it stuck. You built **a token bucket with an injected clock** in *Rate limiting: algorithms
and where they live*. Now write it again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek
at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: "design a rate limiter" is one of the most common system design questions, and the token bucket is
its heart. Reading your old code feels like knowing it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Three layers each try a call up to 3 times. The database is down. How many calls can one user click send to it?
steps.explain: Each layer multiplies the attempts of the one below: 3 × 3 × 3. Retry at one layer, with a budget.

steps.prompt: A breaker is open and its break time has just ended. What happens to the next call?
options: It goes through as a probe with the breaker half-open; its result closes or reopens the breaker
It fails fast, and the breaker stays open until someone resets it
The breaker closes and all queued calls go through at once
steps.explain: Half-open lets a little traffic test the dependency. Letting everything through at once would hit a barely recovered service with the full load.

steps.title: Cold rebuild: TokenBucket
prompt: Write a class `TokenBucket`, from memory (time in seconds is passed in):
- `bool TryTake(double nowSec, double cost = 1)`: refill since the last call (capped at the capacity), then
take `cost` tokens if there are enough;
- `double Tokens(double nowSec)`: refill, then return the tokens;
- a time earlier than the last one seen refills nothing and does not move the last time back.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
